items.q: $(\sec^2\theta - 1)\cos^2\theta = \sin^2\theta$
items.a: $(\sec^2\theta-1)\cos^2\theta=\tan^2\theta\cos^2\theta=\sin^2\theta$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\tan\theta + \sec\theta = \dfrac{1 + \sin\theta}{\cos\theta}$
items.a: $\tan\theta+\sec\theta=\dfrac{\sin\theta+1}{\cos\theta}$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $(\cos\theta - \sin\theta)^2 = 1 - 2\sin\theta\cos\theta$
items.a: $(\cos\theta-\sin\theta)^2=\cos^2\theta+\sin^2\theta-2\sin\theta\cos\theta=1-2\sin\theta\cos\theta$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$
items.a: $\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta=\cos^2\theta-(1-\cos^2\theta)=2\cos^2\theta-1$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\tan\theta + \cot\theta = \sec\theta\,\text{cosec}\,\theta$
items.a: $\dfrac{\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta}=\sec\theta\,\text{cosec}\,\theta$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\dfrac{1 - \sin\theta}{\cos\theta} = \dfrac{\cos\theta}{1 + \sin\theta}$
items.a: $\dfrac{1-\sin\theta}{\cos\theta}\cdot\dfrac{1+\sin\theta}{1+\sin\theta}=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta(1+\sin\theta)}=\dfrac{\cos\theta}{1+\sin\theta}$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\sin\theta\sqrt{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \tan\theta$
items.a: $\sin\theta\sqrt{\sec^2\theta}=\sin\theta\sec\theta=\tan\theta$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\cos\theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2\theta}$
items.a: $\cos^2\theta=1-\sin^2\theta$ and $\cos\theta>0$ for acute $\theta$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $(1 + \cos\theta)(1 - \cos\theta) = \dfrac{1}{\text{cosec}^2\theta}$
items.a: $(1+\cos\theta)(1-\cos\theta)=1-\cos^2\theta=\sin^2\theta=\dfrac{1}{\text{cosec}^2\theta}$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\cos x - \cos x\sin^2 x = \cos^3 x$
items.a: $\cos x(1-\sin^2x)=\cos x\cos^2x=\cos^3x$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} + \dfrac{1 + \cos x}{\sin x} = 2\,\text{cosec}\,x$
items.a: $\dfrac{\sin^2x+(1+\cos x)^2}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=\dfrac{2(1+\cos x)}{\sin x(1+\cos x)}=2\,\text{cosec}\,x$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x} = \dfrac{1 - \cos x}{\sin x}$
items.a: Cross-multiplying: $\sin^2x=(1-\cos x)(1+\cos x)=1-\cos^2x$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\dfrac{1}{1 + \cos a} + \dfrac{1}{1 - \cos a} = 2 + 2\cot^2 a$
items.a: $\dfrac{2}{1-\cos^2a}=2\,\text{cosec}^2a=2+2\cot^2a$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\cos^4 b - \sin^4 b = 1 - 2\sin^2 b$
items.a: $(\cos^2b-\sin^2b)(\cos^2b+\sin^2b)=\cos^2b-\sin^2b=1-2\sin^2b$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\dfrac{\sin y + \cos y}{\sin y} + \dfrac{\cos y - \sin y}{\cos y} = \sec y\,\text{cosec}\,y$
items.a: As printed the identity is false (the left side is $2+\cot y-\tan y$). With the denominators interchanged, $\dfrac{\sin y+\cos y}{\cos y}+\dfrac{\cos y-\sin y}{\sin y}=\tan y+\cot y=\sec y\,\text{cosec}\,y$ (probable misprint).
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $(\sec x - \tan x)^2 = \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{1 + \sin x}$
items.a: $\left(\dfrac{1-\sin x}{\cos x}\right)^2=\dfrac{(1-\sin x)^2}{(1-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}=\dfrac{1-\sin x}{1+\sin x}$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.q: $\sin x\tan x + \cos x = \sec x$.
items.a: $\dfrac{\sin^2x}{\cos x}+\cos x=\dfrac{1}{\cos x}=\sec x$. Proved.
items.e: SpaceBook answer: worked out and checked

items.a: تیل سے بحری و ہوائی جہاز، گاڑیاں، ریلیں، زرعی مشینیں اور کارخانے چلتے ہیں اور تھرمل بجلی بنتی ہے۔ پاکستان اپنی ضرورت کا صرف 10 فیصد تیل پیدا کرتا ہے اور 90 فیصد درآمد کرتا ہے۔ تیل کوٹ سارنگ، توت، میال، کھوڑ، ڈھلیاں (اٹک)، ڈھوڈک (ڈیرہ غازی خان)، کرسال (جہلم)، بدین اور آدھی قاضیاں (راولپنڈی) اور جنوبی سندھ میں ملتا ہے؛ کراچی، حب، ملتان اور راولپنڈی میں تیل صاف کرنے کے کارخانے ہیں۔ ii (ا): قدرتی گیس سب سے پہلے 52-1951ء میں سوئی (بلوچستان) میں دریافت ہوئی؛ گھروں، گاڑیوں، کھاد (29%) اور دوسرے کارخانوں (24%)، سیمنٹ اور تھرمل بجلی میں استعمال؛ ذخائر سوئی، سندھ (خیرپور، مزرانی، کندکوٹ، سارنگ)، پنجاب (ڈھوڈک، ڈھلیاں، میال) اور کرک (گرگری) میں۔ ii (ب): پاکستانی کوئلہ اچھی قسم کا نہیں؛ اینٹوں کے بھٹوں، بجلی اور سیمنٹ میں استعمال؛ مچھ، خوست، ہرنائی، لاکھڑا، مکڑوال، جھمپیر اور تھر سے نکلتا ہے؛ تھر میں تقریباً 175 بلین ٹن ذخائر۔ ii (ج): زراعت معیشت کی ریڑھ کی ہڈی ہے؛ 65% آبادی اس سے وابستہ، قومی دولت کا 32% اور زرِ مبادلہ کا 45% زراعت سے؛ خوراک، چارہ اور صنعتوں کے لیے خام مال فراہم کرتی ہے؛ گندم، چاول، کپاس، گنا اہم فصلیں ہیں۔

items.q: The time required to complete one round trip of a vibrating body is called its:
A simple pendulum has time period T on Earth. On the Moon, where gravity is g/6, its time period will:
Sound waves in air are an example of:
If a wave has a frequency of 50 Hz and a wavelength of 0.4 m, its speed is:
The bending of waves around the edges of an obstacle is known as:
Which of the following is an example of simple harmonic motion?
o: The spinning of Earth on its axis
The motion of a ceiling fan
The motion of a simple pendulum
The bouncing of a ball on the floor
items.e: The motion of a simple pendulum exhibits acceleration directly proportional to displacement and directed towards the mean position for small angles.

items.q: A restoring force in an oscillating spring-mass system is governed by:
items.e: Hooke's Law states F = -kx, where the restoring force is proportional to displacement.

items.q: Which of the following waves requires a material medium for propagation?
items.e: Sound waves are mechanical longitudinal waves that require a solid, liquid, or gas medium to propagate.

items.q: In transverse waves, the distance between two consecutive crests is called:
items.e: Wavelength (λ) is defined as the distance between two consecutive crests or troughs.

items.q: The product of frequency and time period of an oscillating body is always equal to:
items.e: Since f = 1/T, f * T = 1.

items.q: The phenomenon of bending of waves around the corners of obstacles is called:
items.e: Diffraction is the spreading or bending of wave fronts around edges and through narrow slits.

items.q: At the mean position of a body executing SHM, its kinetic energy is:
items.e: At the mean position, speed is maximum, making kinetic energy (1/2 mv²) maximum.

items.q: If 20 waves pass through a point in 2 seconds, the frequency of the wave is:
items.e: Frequency f = N/t = 20 / 2 = 10 Hz.

items.q: Sound waves cannot travel through:
The characteristic of sound that depends upon its frequency is:
The reference intensity of the faintest audible sound (I_0) is:
The minimum distance between a person and a reflecting surface to hear an echo in air at 20°C is:
Sound waves having frequencies higher than 20,000 Hz are termed:
Sound waves in air are characterized as:
items.e: Sound waves in air consist of compressions and rarefactions propagating parallel to particle oscillation.

items.q: The pitch of a sound is determined primarily by its:
items.e: Pitch is the psychological perception of frequency (higher frequency gives higher pitch).

items.q: If the amplitude of a sound wave is tripled, its intensity increases by a factor of:
items.e: Intensity of a wave is directly proportional to the square of its amplitude: I ∝ A²; (3)² = 9.

items.q: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is approximately:
items.e: At 0°C, the speed of sound in dry air at standard atmospheric pressure is 332 m/s.

items.q: A sound level of 0 dB corresponds to:
o: Complete silence with zero sound energy
items.e: 0 dB represents the reference intensity of human hearing threshold, I_0 = 10⁻¹² W/m².

items.q: The minimum time interval required between direct sound and reflected sound for an echo to be distinguished by the human ear is:
items.e: Human auditory persistence lasts about 0.1 second; reflections arriving sooner merge with the original sound.

items.q: The upper frequency limit of the audible range for a healthy young human ear is:
items.e: The audible frequency range extends from 20 Hz up to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz).

items.q: Which technique uses reflected ultrasound pulses to image internal body organs?
items.e: Ultrasonography uses high-frequency sound reflections to generate diagnostic cross-sectional images.

items.q: SONAR stands for:
items.e: SONAR stands for Sound Navigation and Ranging.

items.q: When a sound wave travels from air into water, which of its properties remains unchanged?
items.e: Frequency is determined exclusively by the vibrating source and does not change across media boundaries.

items.q: The focal length of a spherical mirror with radius of curvature 30 cm is:
If the speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m/s and in glass is 2 × 10⁸ m/s, the refractive index of glass is:
The critical angle for a water-air boundary (n_water = 1.33) is approximately:
The image formed by a convex mirror is always:
items.e: Convex mirrors always diverge light rays, producing virtual, upright, and diminished images.

items.q: The relation between focal length f and radius of curvature R of a spherical mirror is:
items.e: Focal length is half of the radius of curvature: f = R/2.

items.q: When a ray of light enters from air into glass, its speed:
items.e: Glass is optically denser than air (n ≈ 1.5), so the speed of light decreases to c/n ≈ 2 × 10⁸ m/s.

items.q: Total internal reflection can occur only when light travels from a:
o: Rarer medium to a denser medium
Denser medium to a rarer medium
items.e: Total internal reflection requires light to travel from an optically denser medium toward a rarer medium at an incident angle greater than the critical angle.

items.q: The unit of optical power of a lens is:
items.e: Optical power is measured in diopters (D), where 1 D = 1 m⁻¹.

items.q: The least distance of distinct vision for a normal human eye is approximately:
items.e: The near point for distinct, comfortable vision in a normal adult eye is 25 cm.

items.q: In a compound microscope, the focal length of the objective lens is:
o: Larger than that of the eyepiece
Smaller than that of the eyepiece
Equal to that of the eyepiece
items.e: The objective lens of a compound microscope has a very short focal length to produce a highly magnified real image.

items.q: Optical fibers work on the principle of:
items.e: Optical fibers transmit light signals through repeated total internal reflection within the higher-index glass core.

items.q: The SI unit of electric charge is:
items.e: The SI unit of charge is the Coulomb (C).

items.q: If the distance between two charged particles is halved, the Coulomb force between them becomes:
items.e: By Coulomb's law F ∝ 1/r^2. When r is halved (r/2), F' = 1/(1/2)^2 = 4F.

items.q: The value of Coulomb constant k depends upon:
o: Material medium and system of units
items.e: The constant k = 1/(4*pi*epsilon) depends on the nature of the medium and the system of units chosen.

items.q: An additional capacitor is added to a group of capacitors already connected in series. The equivalent capacitance will:
items.e: In series combination, 1/Ceq = 1/C1 + 1/C2 + ... Adding another capacitor increases 1/Ceq, which decreases Ceq.

items.q: The SI unit of electric potential is:
items.e: Electric potential V = W/q has unit Joules/Coulomb = Volt (V).

items.q: Four identical 1 μF capacitors are connected together electrically. What is the least possible capacitance of the combination?
items.e: The least capacitance is obtained when all four are connected in series: 1/Ceq = 1+1+1+1 = 4 => Ceq = 1/4 μF.

items.q: Electric field lines around an isolated positive point charge are directed:
items.e: Electric field lines point in the direction of force on a positive test charge, which is radially outward from a positive charge.

items.q: A student needs a 100 Ω resistor for a circuit, but only has a box of 300 Ω resistors. How can she obtain 100 Ω?
items.e: Connecting three identical resistors of 300 Ω in parallel gives Req = 300 / 3 = 100 Ω.

items.q: Which of the following materials is an ohmic conductor at constant temperature?
items.e: Metallic conductors like copper wire obey Ohm's law (linear I-V relationship) at constant temperature.

items.q: The commercial unit of electrical energy is:
items.e: Kilowatt-hour (kWh) is the commercial unit used for electricity billing (1 kWh = 3.6 MJ).

items.q: In a domestic 3-pin plug, the fuse must always be connected in the:
items.e: The fuse must be placed in the live wire to completely disconnect high voltage from the appliance when it blows.

items.q: An electric bulb marked 60 W, 220 V and another marked 100 W, 220 V are connected in parallel to 220 V supply. Which bulb glows brighter?
items.e: In parallel, both receive 220 V. The 100 W bulb consumes more power (P = 100 W > 60 W) and therefore glows brighter.

items.q: What is the frequency of AC supply in Pakistan?
items.e: The standard domestic alternating current frequency in Pakistan is 50 Hz (50 cycles per second).

items.q: When a short circuit occurs, the circuit resistance becomes:
items.e: In a short circuit, live and neutral wires touch directly with near-zero resistance, drawing a huge dangerously high current.

items.q: Which instrument is always connected in series in a circuit to measure current?
items.e: An ammeter has very low resistance and must be connected in series so all current flows through it without significant voltage drop.

items.q: A current carrying wire in which current flows northward is deflected towards east by a magnetic force. The direction of the magnetic field is:
items.e: Using Fleming's Left-Hand Rule: Thumb points East (force), Middle finger points North (current) => Forefinger points straight down.

items.q: The SI unit of mutual inductance, the Henry, is equivalent to:
items.e: From ε = M (ΔI/Δt), M = ε Δt / ΔI => 1 H = 1 V*s / A.

items.q: When the speed at which a magnet is moved through a coil is increased, the induced voltage:
items.e: By Faraday's law, induced EMF is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux (ΔPhi/Δt).

items.q: Continuous slip rings are an essential part of:
items.e: An AC generator uses continuous slip rings and carbon brushes to draw alternating current from the rotating armature.

items.q: A transformer is used for:
items.e: Transformers operate strictly on alternating current because steady direct current does not produce a changing magnetic flux.

items.q: A transformer has a primary winding with 500 turns and a secondary winding with 250 turns. The turns ratio is:
items.e: Turns ratio Ns / Np = 250 / 500 = 0.5.

items.q: If the turns ratio is 5, the secondary voltage is greater than the primary voltage by a factor of:
items.e: Vs / Vp = Ns / Np = 5, so secondary voltage is 5 times greater than primary voltage.

items.q: What is the direction of magnetic field lines inside a solenoid?
o: From North pole to South pole
From South pole to North pole
items.e: Outside a solenoid/magnet, field lines go from North to South; inside they form continuous loops from South to North.

items.q: The process of emission of electrons from a hot metal surface is called:
items.e: Thermionic emission is the liberation of electrons from a heated metallic filament.

items.q: The beam of electrons in a Cathode-Ray Oscilloscope is produced by:
items.e: The electron gun produces, accelerates, and focuses the electron beam.

items.q: When a beam of electrons passes through an electric field, it deflects towards:
items.e: Electrons carry negative charge (-e) and are electrostatically attracted to the positive plate.

items.q: A Cathode-Ray Oscilloscope displays graphs of voltage against:
items.e: The horizontal time-base sweeps the beam across the screen at constant speed, displaying voltage vs time.

items.q: Which of the following is an analogue quantity?
items.e: Air temperature varies continuously over time, making it an analogue quantity.

items.q: The output of a NOT gate is HIGH (1) when its input is:
items.e: A NOT gate is an inverter: an input of 0 produces an output of 1.

items.q: The output of a NOR gate is HIGH (1) only when:
items.e: NOR = NOT(A + B). When A=0 and B=0, A+B=0, and NOT(0) = 1.

items.q: Which logic gate gives output 0 only when all its inputs are 1?
items.e: A NAND gate gives 0 only when A=1 and B=1 (NOT(1.1) = NOT(1) = 0).

items.q: A logic circuit used to sound an alarm when darkness falls uses an LDR and a:
items.e: In darkness, LDR resistance is high and input voltage is LOW (0). A NOT gate inverts 0 to 1, triggering the alarm.

items.q: The scientific method used to store information, arrange it for proper use and communicate it is called:
items.e: Information Technology (IT) is the scientific study and use of systems for storing, retrieving, and sending information.

items.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the five core components of an ICT system?
items.e: The five core components of ICT are: hardware, software, data, procedures, and people.

items.q: Light signals travel through an optical fiber because of:
items.e: Light inside an optical fiber undergoes multiple total internal reflections at the core-cladding boundary.

items.q: In an optical fiber, the refractive index of the core must be:
items.e: Total internal reflection occurs only when light travels from a denser medium (higher n) toward a rarer medium (lower n).

items.q: Which transmission medium transmits data at the highest speed with minimum signal loss?
items.e: Optical fibers offer enormous bandwidth, near-zero electromagnetic interference, and lowest attenuation.

items.q: A compact disc (CD) stores digital data using microscopic:
items.e: Data on optical discs is pressed as a spiral track of microscopic pits and flat lands.

items.q: Which of the following storage devices has no moving mechanical parts?
items.e: USB flash drives and solid-state drives (SSDs) use semiconductor flash memory with zero moving parts.

items.q: The electronic device that converts sound waves into varying electrical audio signals is a:
items.e: A microphone acts as an audio transducer, converting mechanical sound pressure into electrical current.

items.q: What is the primary function of a communication satellite?
items.e: Satellites receive microwave signals from an uplink ground station, amplify them, and retransmit them back to downlink stations.

items.q: Which security measure protects a computer network from unauthorized external internet access?
items.e: A firewall filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on established security rules.

items.q: What is the number of neutrons in the Plutonium nucleus _94^{242}Pu?
items.e: Number of neutrons N = A - Z = 242 - 94 = 148 neutrons.

items.q: Which decay processes (alpha, beta, or gamma) result in a new daughter element?
items.e: Alpha decay changes Z by -2 and beta decay changes Z by +1; gamma decay changes only nuclear energy state.

items.q: What type of nuclear decay leaves the number of protons and neutrons unchanged?
items.e: Gamma emission involves the release of excess nuclear energy without altering Z or A.

items.q: What type of nuclear decay produces the greatest loss of mass and charge?
items.e: Alpha decay ejects a Helium-4 nucleus carrying 4 atomic mass units and +2 elementary charges.

items.q: Polonium-214 (_84^{214}Po) undergoes alpha decay to produce a daughter nucleus that itself undergoes beta decay. Which nucleus ultimately results?
items.e: Alpha decay: _84^{214}Po -> _82^{210}Pb + alpha. Beta decay: _82^{210}Pb -> _83^{210}Bi + beta.

items.q: Radium-226 (_88^{226}Ra) decays by emitting an alpha particle. What is the daughter nucleus?
Krypton-89 is an isotope with a half-life of 269 years. It will reduce to half its original amount in:
items.e: By definition, a radioactive sample reduces to half in exactly one half-life (269 years).

items.q: A sample starts with 1000 radioactive atoms. How many half-lives have elapsed when 750 atoms have decayed?
items.e: Remaining atoms = 1000 - 750 = 250 atoms. 250/1000 = 1/4 = (1/2)^2, so exactly 2.0 half-lives have elapsed.

items.q: The primary origin of energy radiated by the Sun and stars is:
items.e: Hydrogen nuclei fuse into Helium under tremendous core temperature and pressure (thermonuclear fusion).

items.q: Which of the following devices is used to measure radiation exposure for workers in nuclear facilities?
items.e: Radiation workers wear film badge dosimeters or TLD badges to monitor cumulative radiation dose.

items.q: A ship is anchored where the depth of water is 120 m. An ultrasonic signal sent to the bottom of the lake returns in 0.16 s. What is the speed of sound in water?
items.e: The signal travels to the bottom and back, a distance $2d = 2(120) = 240$ m in $0.16$ s, so $v = \dfrac{2d}{t} = \dfrac{240}{0.16} = 1500$ m/s.
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: A gunshot from a 0.22 rimfire rifle has an intensity of about I = (2.5 × 10¹³) W/m². Do we need to wear ear protection? (Considering that prolonged exposure to sounds above 85 decibels can cause hearing damage or loss).
items.a: Yes, ear protection is needed
items.e: $\beta = 10\log_{10}\!\dfrac{I}{I_0} = 10\log_{10}\!\dfrac{2.5\times10^{13}}{1.00\times10^{-12}} = 10\log_{10}(2.5\times10^{25}) \approx 254$ dB (as printed). This is far above 85 dB, so ear protection is certainly required. (The printed intensity looks unrealistically large for a rifle shot; a real shot is about 140 dB, still far above the 85 dB limit.)
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: What sound intensity level in dB is produced by earphones that create an intensity of 4.00 × 10⁻² W/m²? (Use the usual reference level of I₀ = 1.00 × 10⁻¹² W/m².)
items.a: 106 dB
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: Which of the following cannot transmit sound? (A) solid (B) liquid (C) gas (D) vacuum
items.a: D. vacuum
items.e: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material medium (solid, liquid or gas); a vacuum has no particles to vibrate.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: If a ringing bicycle bell is held tightly by hand, it stops producing sound. Why?
items.a: A sounding bell must vibrate freely. When it is held tightly the hand damps (absorbs) its vibrations, so the bell cannot vibrate and no sound is produced.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Why sound cannot be heard on the moon?
items.a: The moon has no atmosphere. Sound needs a material medium to travel, and in the vacuum there is nothing to carry the vibrations, so sound cannot be heard.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: If the speed of sound is dependent on frequency, would music from marching band be enjoyed?
items.a: No. If the speed of sound depended on frequency, notes of different frequency would reach the listener at different times and the music would become distorted. Because in air all frequencies travel at nearly the same speed, the band's music arrives together and is enjoyed.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: What is sound? How it is produced, transmitted and received?
items.a: Sound is a form of energy produced by a vibrating body. Production: a vibrating source (vocal cords, string, tuning fork) disturbs the surrounding particles. Transmission: the disturbance travels as a longitudinal wave of compressions and rarefactions through a material medium (solid, liquid or gas); it cannot travel in a vacuum. Reception: the wave reaches the ear, makes the eardrum vibrate, and the vibrations are passed on to the inner ear and then as signals to the brain.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Various instruments sound different even when they play the same note due to difference in (A) pitch (B) loudness (C) quality (D) intensity
items.a: C. quality
items.e: Quality (timbre) depends on the mixture of harmonics a source produces, so two instruments playing the same note (same pitch and loudness) still sound different.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Describe the terms loudness, pitch and quality. Explain each by giving an example.
items.a: Loudness is the sensation of how strong a sound is; it depends on the intensity (square of the amplitude), e.g. a shout is louder than a whisper. Pitch is the sensation of how high or low a sound is; it depends on the frequency, e.g. a whistle has a higher pitch than a drum. Quality (timbre) is the characteristic that lets us tell two sounds of the same loudness and pitch apart, because of different harmonics, e.g. a sitar and a flute playing the same note.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: The intensity of a sound wave increases by 1000 W/m². What is this increase equal to in decibels? (A) 10 (B) 20 (C) 30 (D) 40
items.a: C. 30 dB
items.e: A rise of 1000 times in intensity changes the level by $\Delta\beta = 10\log_{10}(1000) = 10\times 3 = 30$ dB.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Compared with a sound of 60 decibels, a sound of 80 decibels has an intensity ______ times greater. (A) 10 (B) 100 (C) 1000 (D) 10000
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: The loudness of a sound is most closely related to its ______. (A) frequency (B) period (C) wavelength (D) amplitude
items.a: D. amplitude
items.e: Loudness is the perception of intensity, and intensity is proportional to the square of the amplitude of the wave.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: What is intensity level? Describe the decibels scale for the intensity of different sound levels.
items.a: Intensity is the sound energy passing per second through a unit area perpendicular to the direction of travel, $I = P/A$ in W/m². Intensity level $\beta = 10\log_{10}(I/I_0)$ in decibels (dB), where $I_0 = 10^{-12}$ W/m² is the threshold of hearing. Each increase of 10 dB means ten times the intensity. Examples: whisper 30 dB, normal conversation 60 dB, heavy traffic 80 dB, jet engine 120 dB, and about 120-130 dB is the threshold of pain.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: The sound intensity 3 m from a jackhammer is 8.20 × 10⁻² W/m². What is the sound intensity level in decibels? (Use the usual reference level of I₀ = 1.00 × 10⁻¹² W/m².)
items.a: 109 dB
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: An echo occurs when a sound wave is ... (A) absorbed (B) transmitted (C) refracted (D) reflected
items.a: D. reflected
items.e: An echo is the repetition of a sound heard after the sound wave is reflected from a hard, distant surface.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: The speed of sound on a warm day when the outdoor temperature is 38°C is (A) 331 m/s (B) 345 m/s (C) 354 m/s (D) 362 m/s
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Minimum echo distance is reduced in (A) summer (B) winter (C) spring (D) space
items.a: B. winter
items.e: The minimum echo distance is $d = v t/2$ with $t = 0.1$ s, so it is smaller when the speed of sound is smaller. Sound travels slower in cold air, so the minimum distance is reduced in winter.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Why is the intensity of an echo less than that of the original sound?
items.a: Part of the sound energy is absorbed by the reflecting surface, and the reflected wave spreads over a larger area as it travels back (intensity falls with the square of the distance), so the echo is weaker than the original sound.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: In which medium air or water, an echo is heard sooner? Why?
items.a: In water. Sound travels about 1500 m/s in water but only about 340 m/s in air, so the reflected sound returns sooner and the echo is heard earlier.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: If a person places his ear on rails of railroad for determination of coming train. Why is this done, and how does it work?
items.a: Sound travels much faster and with less loss in steel (about 5000 m/s) than in air (about 340 m/s). The rails carry the vibrations of the approaching train long before the sound arrives through air, so the person hears the train earlier and can judge that it is coming.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: When you watch a thunderstorm, you see the lightning first, and you hear the thunder afterward. Why is the thunder delayed?
items.a: Light travels at $3\times10^{8}$ m/s, so the flash reaches us almost instantly, while sound travels only about 340 m/s. The thunder is delayed by the time $t = d/v$ the sound needs to cover the distance to the storm.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Why does your voice sound fuller in the shower?
items.a: The hard, smooth walls of a shower reflect sound with little absorption. The reflected sound reaches the ear almost at once and merges with the original sound (reverberation), which makes the voice sound louder and fuller.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Why is it so quiet after a snowfall?
items.a: Fresh snow is soft and porous with a lot of trapped air. It absorbs sound instead of reflecting it, so there is almost no reflection or reverberation and the surroundings become very quiet.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: What is the speed of sound?
items.a: The speed of sound is the distance a sound wave travels in one second, $v = f\lambda$. In air at 0 °C it is about 331 m/s and increases by about 0.6 m/s for each °C: $v = 331 + 0.6\,T$. It is greater in liquids (about 1500 m/s in water) and greatest in solids (about 5000 m/s in steel).
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: How sound is reflected? Describe the difference between echo and reverberation.
items.a: Sound is reflected when it strikes a hard surface (wall, cliff) and obeys the laws of reflection. An echo is a reflected sound heard separately after the original sound; it needs a reflecting surface at least about 17 m away (the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later). Reverberation is the persistence of sound in a room caused by many reflections that arrive less than 0.1 s apart and blend with the original sound, so there is no separate repetition.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: What is the speed of sound in air at −20°C?
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: Army man wearing binoculars see the flash from enemy tank fire 5 s before the fire is heard, he records 26°C temperature on his personal thermometer. What is the distance of the tank from him?
items.a: About 1.73 km
items.e: At 26 °C, $v = 331 + 0.6(26) = 346.6$ m/s. The flash arrives practically at once, so $d = vt = 346.6\times5 \approx 1733$ m $\approx 1.73$ km.
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: Calculate the wavelengths of sounds at the extremes of the audible range, 20 Hz and 20,000 Hz, at normal room temperature of 20°C?
items.a: 17.2 m and 1.7 cm
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: Ishfaq stands between two high rise buildings A and B, such that he is at 33 m distance from building A. When he blows the whistle, he hears the first echo after 0.2 s and second echo after 0.8 s. Calculate (a) the speed of sound and (b) distance of building B from him.
items.e: (a) The first echo comes from building A: the sound travels $2\times33 = 66$ m in 0.2 s, so $v = 66/0.2 = 330$ m/s. (b) The second echo comes from building B: $2d = vt = 330\times0.8 = 264$ m, so $d = 132$ m.
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: What is noise? Explain why noise is nuisance?
items.a: Noise is an unwanted, unpleasant sound with irregular vibrations (traffic, machines, loudspeakers). It is a nuisance because it disturbs sleep, concentration and conversation, causes stress and headaches and, if loud or prolonged (above about 85 dB), can damage hearing.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: What is acoustic protection? Why is it important?
items.a: Acoustic protection is the control of sound so that unwanted noise is reduced and wanted sound is heard clearly: using sound-absorbing materials (carpets, curtains, foam, acoustic tiles), double walls and windows, ear plugs or ear muffs and sound barriers. It is important to protect hearing and health, to reduce noise pollution and to give good sound quality in halls and studios.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Humans can hear sound that is (A) less than 20 Hz (B) between 20 Hz and 20 kHz (C) greater than 20 kHz (D) None
items.a: B. between 20 Hz and 20 kHz
items.e: The audible range of the human ear is about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz; below it is infrasound and above it is ultrasound.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Why sound produced by a simple pendulum is not heard?
items.a: A simple pendulum oscillates about once per second (frequency of about 1 Hz). This is far below 20 Hz, the lower limit of human hearing (infrasound), so the sound it produces cannot be heard.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: What is audible frequency range?
items.a: The audible range is the range of frequencies the human ear can hear, about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz). Sounds below 20 Hz are infrasound and above 20 kHz are ultrasound; both are inaudible to humans.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Suppose that you were handed a lens and a ruler and told to determine the focal length of the lens. How would you proceed?
items.a: Focus the light of a distant object (the sun or a far window) on a sheet of paper or a wall. When the image is sharpest, measure the distance from the lens to the image with the ruler; this is the focal length. Alternatively measure an object distance and the sharp image distance and use $1/f = 1/d_o + 1/d_i$.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Will a nearsighted person who wears corrective lenses in her glasses be able to see clearly underwater when wearing those glasses?
items.a: No. Her spectacles are shaped for use in air; under water the difference between the refractive index of glass (about 1.5) and water (1.33) is small, so the lenses bend light much less, and the eye itself loses most of its focusing power. She will not see clearly.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: In blind turns on hilly roads, mirrors are used to help drivers. Are these mirrors plane mirrors, concave mirrors or convex mirrors? Explain.
items.a: Convex mirrors. They give a wide field of view and an upright, smaller image, so the driver can see traffic coming around the bend from a long way off; plane mirrors give a narrow view and concave mirrors give an inverted or magnified view.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: If the angle of incidence is 30° then the angle of reflection will be (A) 30° (B) 45° (C) 90° (D) 210°
items.e: By the law of reflection the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 30°.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: What is meant by reflection of light? State and explain laws of reflection with diagrams.
items.a: Reflection is the bouncing back of light when it strikes a surface. Laws: (1) the incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence lie in the same plane; (2) the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, $\theta_i = \theta_r$. (Diagram: a ray AO hits the mirror at O; the normal ON is perpendicular to the surface; the reflected ray OB makes the angle $\theta_r = \theta_i$ with ON.)
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Which type of lens would you use to start fire from light from sun concave or convex, would work best? At what distance from the lens should the paper be held for best results?
items.a: A convex (converging) lens works best, because it brings the parallel rays of the sun to a point. The paper should be held at the focal point, a distance equal to the focal length behind the lens, where the bright spot is smallest and hottest.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: When r is the radius of curvature of concave mirror. Real diminished image will be formed when the object is at (A) dₒ > r (B) dₒ = r (C) r > dₒ > f (D) dₒ = f
items.a: A. $d_o > r$
items.e: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, diminished image between F and C when the object is beyond the centre of curvature (object distance greater than $r$).
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: The focal length of convex mirror with radius of curvature 10 cm is (A) +10 cm (B) +5 cm (C) −10 cm (D) −5 cm
items.a: D. −5 cm
items.e: $f = r/2 = 10/2 = 5$ cm, and the focus of a convex mirror is virtual (behind the mirror), so with the sign convention $f = -5$ cm.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: An object is placed 7 cm from a concave mirror whose radius of curvature is 10 cm, the image formed will be (A) real and upright (B) virtual and upright (C) real and inverted (D) virtual and inverted
items.a: C. real and inverted
items.e: The focal length is $f = r/2 = 5$ cm. An object at 7 cm lies between F and C (5 cm < 7 cm < 10 cm), so the image is real, inverted and magnified, formed beyond C.
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: Are rearview mirrors used in cars concave or convex?
items.a: Convex mirrors. They give a wide field of view and an upright, diminished image of the traffic behind the car.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Derive spherical mirror formula.
items.a: For an object of height $h_o$ at distance $d_o$ from a concave mirror, the image has height $h_i$ at distance $d_i$. Two similar triangles (the ray striking the pole P and the ray through the centre of curvature C) give $\dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o}$ and, from the triangles at the focus F, $\dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = -\dfrac{f}{d_o - f}$. Equating, $\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} = \dfrac{f}{d_o - f}$, which gives $d_i(d_o - f) = f d_o$ and so $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{d_o} + \dfrac{1}{d_i}$, the mirror equation. Magnification: $m = \dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o}$.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: A 1.50 cm-high object is placed 20.0 cm from a concave mirror with radius of curvature 30.0 cm. Determine (a) the position of the image, and (b) its size, also draw the ray diagrams.
items.a: (a) 60 cm in front of the mirror (b) 4.5 cm, inverted
items.e: $f = R/2 = 15.0$ cm. (a) $\dfrac{1}{d_i} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{d_o} = \dfrac{1}{15.0} - \dfrac{1}{20.0} = \dfrac{1}{60}$, so $d_i = 60$ cm, a real image in front of the mirror. (b) $m = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} = -\dfrac{60}{20} = -3$, so $h_i = m h_o = -3(1.50) = -4.5$ cm: the image is 4.5 cm high, real and inverted. (Ray diagram: parallel ray through F after reflection; ray through F parallel after reflection; ray to the pole; they meet at 60 cm.)
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: A candle of height 8.0 cm is located at a distance of 300 mm from a convex mirror, its virtual image is formed behind the mirror at a distance of 3.0 cm from the pole (or vertex). Find the focal length of the mirror and height of the image formed.
items.e: $d_o = 300$ mm $= 30$ cm and the virtual image is behind the mirror, $d_i = -3.0$ cm. $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{d_o} + \dfrac{1}{d_i} = \dfrac{1}{30} - \dfrac{1}{3.0} = \dfrac{1 - 10}{30} = -\dfrac{9}{30}$, so $f = -3.33$ cm. $m = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} = \dfrac{3.0}{30} = 0.10$, so $h_i = 0.10\times 8.0 = 0.8$ cm (upright and diminished).
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: Which one of the following materials will refract light more (A) water (B) glass (C) air (D) diamond
items.a: D. diamond
items.e: A material refracts light more when its refractive index is larger. Diamond (n ≈ 2.42) has a higher index than glass (≈ 1.5), water (1.33) or air (1.0003).
items.h: MULTIPLE CHOICE QUESTIONS

items.q: A magician during a show makes a glass lens with n = 1.47 disappear in a trough of liquid. What is the refractive index of the liquid? Could the liquid be water?
items.a: The lens disappears when the liquid has the same refractive index as the glass, so no refraction occurs at the surface: the liquid has $n = 1.47$. It could not be water, because water has $n = 1.33$.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Can we achieve total internal reflection from optically rare medium to optically dense medium?
items.a: No. Total internal reflection happens only when light travels from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium ($n_1 > n_2$) at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle. Going from rare to dense, the ray bends towards the normal and is always refracted.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: What is meant by refraction of light? What is the index of refraction? State and explain laws of refraction with diagrams.
items.a: Refraction is the change of direction of light when it passes from one transparent medium to another because its speed changes. The index of refraction is $n = c/v$, the ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to its speed in the medium. Laws (Snell): (1) the incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal lie in the same plane; (2) $n_1\sin\theta_1 = n_2\sin\theta_2$, i.e. the ratio $\sin\theta_1/\sin\theta_2$ is constant for the two media. A ray entering a denser medium bends towards the normal; entering a rarer medium it bends away.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Calculate the speed of light in zircon with index of refraction n = 1.923, a material used in jewelry to replicate diamond.
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: A light ray strikes an air/water surface at an angle of 46° with respect to the normal. The refractive index for water is 1.33. Find the angle of refraction when the direction of the ray is (a) from air to water and (b) from water to air.
items.e: (a) Air to water: $\sin\theta_2 = \dfrac{\sin 46^\circ}{1.33} = \dfrac{0.7193}{1.33} = 0.5408$, so $\theta_2 = 32.7^\circ$. (b) Water to air: $n_1\sin 46^\circ = n_2\sin\theta_2$ gives $\sin\theta_2 = 1.33\times0.7193 = 0.9567$, so $\theta_2 = 73.1^\circ$ (the critical angle of water is 48.8°, so 46° is below it and the ray emerges).
items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: What is total internal reflection? How we can calculate the critical angle for total internal reflection? What are the conditions for total internal reflection?
items.a: Total internal reflection (TIR) is the complete reflection of light back into the denser medium when it meets a boundary with a rarer medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle. The critical angle is the angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction is 90°: $\sin\theta_c = n_2/n_1$ ($n_1 > n_2$). Conditions: (1) light must travel from a denser to a rarer medium; (2) the angle of incidence must be greater than the critical angle.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: What are optical fibres? Give some applications of optical fibers.
items.a: An optical fibre is a thin, flexible strand of glass or plastic made of a core surrounded by a cladding of lower refractive index. Light entering one end is carried to the other by repeated total internal reflections at the core-cladding boundary with very little loss. Applications: telephone, television and internet communication cables, medical endoscopes to look inside the body, laser surgery, decorative lamps and sensors.
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: Describe the behavior for a ray of light after passing through a prism.
items.a: When a ray of light passes through a glass prism it is refracted at both faces, bending towards the base each time, so the emergent ray is deviated from the incident direction. White light also splits into its seven colours (dispersion) because each colour has a different speed in glass and therefore a different refractive index: red is bent least and violet most, giving a spectrum.

items.q: If a concave mirror produces a real image, is the image necessarily inverted? Explain.
items.a: Yes. A real image is formed where light rays actually meet, and for a concave mirror (object outside the focal length) a real image is always inverted. Only a virtual image, formed with the object inside F, is upright.
items.h: CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS. Give a brief response to the following questions

items.q: Derive thin lens equation.
items.a: For a thin lens, an object of height $h_o$ at distance $d_o$ forms an image of height $h_i$ at distance $d_i$. Using similar triangles formed by the ray through the optical centre and the ray through the focus, $\dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = \dfrac{d_i}{d_o}$ and $\dfrac{h_i}{h_o} = \dfrac{d_i - f}{f}$. Equating, $\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} = \dfrac{d_i - f}{f}$, so $f d_i = d_o d_i - f d_o$; dividing by $d_o d_i f$ gives $\dfrac{1}{d_o} + \dfrac{1}{d_i} = \dfrac{1}{f}$, the thin-lens equation (with the sign convention, the magnification is $m = -d_i/d_o$).

items.q: Describe power of lens and its resolving power. What are its units?
items.a: The power of a lens is its ability to bend light and is $P = 1/f$ with $f$ in metres; its unit is the dioptre (D = m⁻¹). A converging lens has positive power and a diverging lens negative power. The resolving power is the ability of an optical instrument to show two close objects as separate; it is the reciprocal of the smallest angle $\theta$ that can be resolved, $\theta \approx 1.22\lambda/D$, so it increases with a larger aperture $D$ and shorter wavelength. Its unit is the reciprocal of radian (rad⁻¹).
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: How the human eye works? How the defects in the eye like short sightedness and long sightedness be corrected by using lenses?
items.a: The eye is a lens system: light enters through the cornea and pupil (the iris controls its size), the eye lens focuses it, and a real, inverted image forms on the retina; the optic nerve carries the signal to the brain, which interprets it as upright. The ciliary muscles change the shape of the lens to focus near and far objects (accommodation). Short sightedness (myopia): the image forms in front of the retina, so distant objects are blurred; it is corrected with a concave (diverging) lens. Long sightedness (hypermetropia): the image forms behind the retina, so near objects are blurred; it is corrected with a convex (converging) lens.

items.q: What is a simple microscope? Using a ray diagram explain its working, angular magnification and magnifying power.
items.a: A simple microscope is a single convex lens of short focal length used as a magnifying glass. The object is placed inside the focal length, so the lens forms an upright, enlarged, virtual image at the near point (25 cm). Angular magnification $M = \theta'/\theta$; for the image at the near point $M = 1 + \dfrac{N}{f}$ with $N = 25$ cm, and for the image at infinity $M = N/f$. (Ray diagram: the object lies between F and the lens; the rays diverge after the lens and appear to come from a larger image behind the object.)
items.h: COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS. Give an extended response to the following questions

items.q: What is a compound microscope? Using a ray diagram for a compound microscope, mention its magnifying power.
items.a: A compound microscope uses two convex lenses: an objective of very short focal length that forms a real, inverted, magnified image of the object, and an eyepiece that acts as a magnifier of this image and gives a final virtual, inverted, highly magnified image. The total magnifying power is the product of the two magnifications, $M = m_o \times M_e = \left(-\dfrac{d_i}{d_o}\right)\left(1 + \dfrac{N}{f_e}\right)$; for a long tube it is about $M \approx -\dfrac{L N}{f_o f_e}$.

items.h: NUMERICAL QUESTIONS

items.q: What is a telescope? Using a ray diagram explain its working, angular magnification and magnifying power.
items.a: A telescope is an optical instrument that makes distant objects look nearer and bigger. A refracting (astronomical) telescope has an objective lens of long focal length $f_o$ that forms a real image of the distant object at its focal point, and an eyepiece of short focal length $f_e$ that magnifies this image; the lens separation is $L = f_o + f_e$ for the image at infinity. The angular magnification (magnifying power) is $M = \dfrac{\theta'}{\theta} = \dfrac{f_o}{f_e}$ (the final image is inverted).

items.q: What is electric charge? How objects can be electrified? Describe with the help of experiments.

items.q3: برېښنايي چارج څه دی؟ شیان څنګه برېښنايي کېږي؟ د تجربو په مرسته یې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Electric charge is the property of matter that makes it experience a force in an electric field; it is of two kinds, positive and negative, measured in coulombs (C). Objects are electrified by friction, conduction and induction. Experiment: rub a glass rod with silk and an ebonite rod with fur; each rod then picks up small pieces of paper, and a hanging glass rod is repelled by another rubbed glass rod but attracted by a rubbed ebonite rod. This shows two kinds of charge: like charges repel and unlike charges attract. In friction, electrons move from one material to the other, so one becomes positive and the other negative; in conduction a charged body touching a neutral one shares its charge with it.

items.a: Electrostatic induction is the process of charging a conductor without touching it. Bring a negatively charged rod near, but not touching, an insulated neutral metal sphere: electrons in the sphere are repelled to the far side, so the near side becomes positive and the far side negative. If the far side is earthed (touched by a finger) the repelled electrons flow to the ground; removing the earth connection first and then the rod leaves the sphere with a net positive charge, opposite to that of the rod.

items.a: The electric field is the region around a charge in which another charge experiences a force. Field lines of an isolated positive point charge point radially outward and those of an isolated negative charge point radially inward; the lines never cross, they start on positive and end on negative charges, and they are closer together where the field is stronger.

items.a: Lightning occurs when friction between ice particles and air in a storm cloud separates charge: the cloud bottom becomes negative and induces positive charge on the ground. When the potential difference becomes very large the air breaks down and charge flows in a giant spark. Safety: stay inside a building or a car, avoid open fields, tall trees and water, do not use metal objects or phones outdoors, and fit buildings with lightning rods connected to the ground.

items.a: In a series combination the capacitors are connected end to end so that the same charge $Q$ is on each, while the potential differences add up, $V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3$. Since $V = Q/C$, $\dfrac{Q}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{Q}{C_1} + \dfrac{Q}{C_2} + \dfrac{Q}{C_3}$, so $\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2} + \dfrac{1}{C_3}$. The equivalent capacitance is smaller than the smallest capacitor.

items.q: What is potential difference and emf? Differentiate between them.
items.q2: پوٹینشل ڈفرنس اور emf کیا ہیں؟ ان میں فرق بیان کریں۔
items.q3: د پوټانشیل توپیر او emf څه دي؟ توپیر یې ووایئ.
items.a: Potential difference is the work done per unit charge in moving a charge between two points of a circuit, $V = W/Q$; it is the energy transferred to the load. The emf of a source is the total energy supplied per unit charge by the source (including the energy used in driving charge through the cell's own internal resistance). Difference: emf is the cause that drives the current and is measured when no current flows (open circuit), whereas potential difference is the effect measured across a component, and it is less than the emf when current flows because of the internal resistance. Both are measured in volts.

items.a: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge through a conductor, $I = Q/t$. Its unit is the ampere (A): 1 A = 1 C/s. By convention the direction of conventional current is from the positive to the negative terminal of the battery (the direction positive charges would move), whereas the electrons in a metal actually move in the opposite direction, from negative to positive.

items.q: State and explain Ohm's Law. What are its limitations?
items.q2: اوہم کا قانون بیان اور واضح کریں۔ اس کی حدود کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: د اوم قانون ووایئ او تشریح یې کړئ. محدودیتونه یې څه دي؟
items.a: Ohm's law: the current through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends provided temperature and other physical conditions stay constant, $V \propto I$ or $V = IR$, where $R$ is the resistance. A graph of V against I is a straight line through the origin. Limitations: it holds only for ohmic (metallic) conductors at constant temperature; it does not apply to devices such as diodes, thermistors, filament lamps, transistors and electrolytes, where V-I is not linear.

items.q: What is resistance and in what units we measure resistance?

items.a: Resistance is the opposition a conductor offers to the flow of current, $R = V/I$. Its unit is the ohm (Ω): 1 Ω = 1 V/A.

items.q: What is series combination of resistors? How we can determine equivalent resistance for different resistors connected in series?
items.q2: مزاحمتوں کا سلسلہ وار ملاپ کیا ہے؟ سلسلہ وار جڑی مختلف مزاحمتوں کی مساوی مزاحمت کیسے معلوم کی جاتی ہے؟
items.q3: د مقاومتونو لړۍ ییز ترکیب څه دی؟ د لړۍ ییزو مقاومتونو معادل مقاومت څنګه معلومېږي؟
items.a: In a series combination the resistors are joined end to end, so the same current $I$ flows through each and the voltages add: $V = V_1 + V_2 + V_3 = IR_1 + IR_2 + IR_3 = IR_{eq}$. Hence $R_{eq} = R_1 + R_2 + R_3$. The equivalent resistance is greater than the largest resistor.

items.q: What is parallel combination of resistors? How we can determine equivalent resistance for different resistors connected in parallel?
items.q2: مزاحمتوں کا متوازی ملاپ کیا ہے؟ متوازی جڑی مختلف مزاحمتوں کی مساوی مزاحمت کیسے معلوم کی جاتی ہے؟
items.q3: د مقاومتونو موازي ترکیب څه دی؟ د موازي مقاومتونو معادل مقاومت څنګه معلومېږي؟
items.a: In a parallel combination the resistors are connected across the same two points, so each has the same potential difference $V$ and the currents add: $I = I_1 + I_2 + I_3$. Since $I = V/R$, $\dfrac{V}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{V}{R_1} + \dfrac{V}{R_2} + \dfrac{V}{R_3}$, so $\dfrac{1}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dfrac{1}{R_3}$. The equivalent resistance is smaller than the smallest resistor.

items.q: Explain the factors on which the resistance of metallic conductor depends.
items.q2: ان عوامل کی وضاحت کریں جن پر دھاتی موصل کی مزاحمت منحصر ہے۔
items.q3: هغه عوامل تشریح کړئ چې د فلزي هادي مقاومت پرې اړه لري.
items.a: The resistance of a metallic wire depends on (1) its length $L$: $R \propto L$; (2) its cross-sectional area $A$: $R \propto 1/A$ (a thicker wire has less resistance); (3) the material, through its resistivity $\rho$; and (4) its temperature: resistance of metals rises with temperature. Together $R = \rho\dfrac{L}{A}$.

items.q: What are ohmic and non-ohmic devices? Sketch and interpret the V-I characteristic graph to justify metallic conductor, filament lamp and thermistor as ohmic or non-ohmic materials.
items.q2: اوہمک اور غیر اوہمک آلات کیا ہیں؟ دھاتی موصل، فلامنٹ لیمپ اور تھرمسٹر کو اوہمک یا غیر اوہمک ثابت کرنے کے لیے V-I خصوصیاتی گراف بنا کر واضح کریں۔
items.q3: اومیک او غیر اومیک وسیلې څه دي؟ د فلزي هادي، فلامنټ څراغ او ترمیستور د اومیک یا غیر اومیک ثابتولو لپاره د V-I ګراف رسم او تشریح کړئ.
items.a: Ohmic devices obey Ohm's law, so their V-I graph is a straight line through the origin (resistance constant); non-ohmic devices do not obey it and their V-I graph is curved. A metallic conductor at constant temperature gives a straight line: ohmic. A filament lamp gives a curve that bends towards the voltage axis because the filament heats up and its resistance increases: non-ohmic. A thermistor gives a curve bending towards the current axis because its resistance falls as it heats: non-ohmic.

items.q: Differentiate between alternating current and direct current.

items.a: Direct current (DC) flows in one direction only, with constant polarity (cells, batteries, solar cells); its graph against time is a straight line. Alternating current (AC) reverses its direction periodically (50 Hz in Pakistan) and varies sinusoidally; it comes from AC generators and the mains supply. AC is easily changed in voltage by transformers and transmitted over long distances; DC is needed for electronics and battery charging.

items.q: State the functions of live, neutral and earth wires in domestic main supply.
items.q2: گھریلو مین سپلائی میں لائیو، نیوٹرل اور ارتھ تاروں کے کام بیان کریں۔

items.a: The live wire (brown) carries current from the supply to the appliance at high potential through the fuse and switch. The neutral wire (blue) completes the circuit by returning the current to the supply at about zero potential. The earth wire (green/yellow) is connected to the metal case of the appliance and to the ground; if a fault touches the case to the live wire, a large current flows to earth, blowing the fuse and protecting the user from shock.

items.q: Differentiate between electric and magnetic fields.

items.a: Electromagnetic induction is the production of an emf (and current) in a conductor when the magnetic flux linked with it changes (Faraday). It occurs, for example, when a magnet is pushed into or pulled out of a coil. Factors: (1) the speed of relative motion of the magnet and coil (faster change gives larger emf); (2) the strength of the magnet; (3) the number of turns of the coil; (4) the area of the coil. Faraday's law: $\varepsilon = -N\dfrac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t}$.

items.a: Lenz's law gives the direction of the induced emf: it acts in such a direction that the magnetic field of the induced current opposes the change in flux that produced it (the minus sign in Faraday's law). For example, pushing the north pole of a magnet into a coil makes the near end of the coil a north pole, which repels the magnet; work has to be done against this repulsion, and that work appears as electrical energy. If the induced current helped the change, energy would be created from nothing, so Lenz's law is an expression of conservation of energy.

items.a: Mutual induction is the production of an emf in one coil (secondary) when the current in a neighbouring coil (primary) changes, because the changing magnetic flux of the primary links with the secondary. The induced emf is $\varepsilon_s = -M\dfrac{\Delta I_p}{\Delta t}$, where $M$ is the mutual inductance, measured in henry (H). It is the principle of the transformer.

items.a: Cathode rays are streams of fast-moving electrons that travel from the cathode in a vacuum tube. They are produced when a hot cathode emits electrons by thermionic emission and a high voltage between the cathode and the anode accelerates them. Properties: they travel in straight lines, carry negative charge (deflected by electric and magnetic fields), produce fluorescence on a screen, and can produce X-rays when they hit a metal target.

items.a: An electric field deflects the electron beam towards the positive plate, in the direction opposite to the field, with a force $F = eE$. These effects are used to move the beam on the screen of a CRO.

items.a: A CRO consists of an electron gun, deflecting plates (X and Y plates) and a fluorescent screen in an evacuated tube. The electron beam makes a bright spot on the screen. A voltage on the Y plates moves the spot vertically and the time-base (a saw-tooth voltage) on the X plates sweeps it horizontally, so a waveform of voltage against time is displayed. Uses: measuring voltage, time period and frequency of signals, displaying waveforms, testing electronic circuits and, in medicine, ECG and EEG displays.

items.q3: د انالوګ او ډیجیټل الکترونیک ترمنځ څه توپیر دی؟
items.a: Analogue electronics deals with signals that vary continuously in value (like the sound wave from a microphone), while digital electronics deals with signals that have only two levels, high (1) and low (0). Digital circuits are less affected by noise, easier to store and process (computers, mobile phones), while analogue circuits represent the real signal directly (old radio, record players).

items.a: A logic gate is an electronic circuit with one or more inputs and a single output that follows a logical rule. AND: output 1 only when all inputs are 1 ($X = A\cdot B$). OR: output 1 when any input is 1 ($X = A + B$). NOT: output is the opposite of the input ($X = \overline{A}$). NAND: AND followed by NOT; output 0 only when all inputs are 1 ($X = \overline{AB}$). NOR: OR followed by NOT; output 1 only when all inputs are 0 ($X = \overline{A+B}$). Truth tables, inputs A B giving output: AND 00→0, 01→0, 10→0, 11→1; OR 00→0, 01→1, 10→1, 11→1; NAND 00→1, 01→1, 10→1, 11→0; NOR 00→1, 01→0, 10→0, 11→0; NOT 0→1, 1→0.

items.q: What is nucleus? How a nuclide is represented symbolically?
items.q2: مرکزہ کیا ہے؟ نیوکلائیڈ کو علامتی طور پر کیسے ظاہر کیا جاتا ہے؟
items.q3: هسته څه ده؟ نیوکلایډ په سمبولیک ډول څنګه ښودل کېږي؟
items.a: The nucleus is the small, dense, positively charged centre of an atom containing protons and neutrons (nucleons); it holds nearly all of the mass of the atom. A nuclide is written as ${}^{A}_{Z}X$, where X is the chemical symbol, $Z$ the atomic (proton) number and $A$ the mass (nucleon) number; the number of neutrons is $N = A - Z$. Example: ${}^{14}_{6}C$ has 6 protons and 8 neutrons.

items.q2: تابکاری کیا ہے؟ تین قسم کے تابکار اخراج کی نوعیت، آئنائزنگ اور نفوذ کی صلاحیتیں بیان کریں۔
items.q3: راډیواکټیویټي څه ده؟ د دریو ډوله راډیواکټیو خپرونو طبیعت، ایونایزینګ او نفوذ وړتیاوې بیان کړئ.
items.a: Radioactivity is the spontaneous emission of radiation from unstable nuclei. Alpha ($\alpha$): a helium nucleus (2 protons + 2 neutrons), charge +2, strongly ionizing, least penetrating (stopped by paper). Beta ($\beta$): fast electrons, charge −1, medium ionizing, stopped by a few mm of aluminium. Gamma ($\gamma$): electromagnetic waves of very high energy, no charge, weakly ionizing, most penetrating (reduced only by thick lead or concrete).

items.q2: مرکزی تبدیلیاں کیا ہیں؟ الفا یا بیٹا ذرات کے اخراج پر مرکزے کی ترکیب میں کیا تبدیلیاں دیکھی جاتی ہیں؟ علامتی مساواتوں سے وضاحت کریں۔
items.q3: هستوي بدلونونه څه دي؟ کله چې الفا یا بېټا ذرې خپرې شي د هستې په ترکیب کې کوم بدلونونه لیدل کېږي؟ په سمبولیکو معادلو یې تشریح کړئ.
items.a: A nuclear transmutation is the change of one element into another when the nucleus emits a particle. Alpha emission: the nucleus loses 2 protons and 2 neutrons, so $Z$ decreases by 2 and $A$ by 4, e.g. ${}^{238}_{92}U \rightarrow {}^{234}_{90}Th + {}^{4}_{2}He$. Beta emission: a neutron changes into a proton and an electron, so $Z$ increases by 1 and $A$ stays the same, e.g. ${}^{14}_{6}C \rightarrow {}^{14}_{7}N + {}^{0}_{-1}e$.

items.a: The half life is the time taken for half of the radioactive nuclei in a sample to decay (equivalently, for the activity to fall to half). After one half life half remains, after two half lives a quarter, after three an eighth. For example, if the half life is 5 days, 80 g of the sample becomes 40 g after 5 days and 20 g after 10 days.

items.a: Radioisotopes are isotopes of an element whose nuclei are radioactive. Uses: in medicine (cobalt-60 for cancer treatment, iodine-131 for the thyroid, technetium-99m for scans), in industry (checking thickness and leaks in pipes, gauges), in agriculture (tracers, crop improvement, preserving food), in archaeology (carbon dating) and in sterilizing medical equipment.

items.q2: لکڑی، ہڈیوں اور دیگر نوادرات کی عمر معلوم کرنے کے لیے کاربن-14 کیسے استعمال ہوتا ہے؟

items.a: Living plants and animals take in carbon-14 along with ordinary carbon, so their C-14 to C-12 ratio is fixed. When they die, no new C-14 is taken in and the C-14 decays with a half life of 5730 years. By measuring the fraction of C-14 left in a wooden, bone or fibre sample and comparing it with that in living matter, the number of half lives that have passed, and so its age, can be calculated.

items.q: What are fission and fusion?
items.q2: انشقاق اور ادغام کیا ہیں؟
items.q3: فیشن او فیوژن څه دي؟
items.a: Fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus (e.g. uranium-235) into two lighter nuclei, after absorbing a neutron, with release of a large amount of energy and more neutrons; it is the basis of nuclear reactors and atomic bombs. Fusion is the joining of two light nuclei (e.g. hydrogen isotopes) to form a heavier nucleus, releasing even more energy per unit mass; it needs very high temperature and pressure and takes place in the sun and stars.

items.a: Background radiation is the low level of ionizing radiation that is always present around us. Natural sources: cosmic rays from space, radioactive rocks and soil (radon gas, uranium, thorium), building materials and the food and water we take (potassium-40, carbon-14). Artificial sources: medical X-rays, nuclear power and fallout from weapons testing. Natural sources give most of the exposure.

items.a: 1 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے بھلا تم دیکھو اگر اللہ تمھارے کان اور تمھاری آنکھیں لے لے اور تمھارے دلوں پر مہر لگا دے (تو) اللہ کے سوا کون معبود ہے جو یہ (نعمتیں) تمھارے پاس لے آئے؟ آپ دیکھیے ہم کس کس طرح اپنی آیتیں بیان کرتے ہیں پھر بھی وہ منھ موڑ لیتے ہیں۔ (ب): رسول صرف خوش خبری سنانے والے اور ڈرانے والے بنا کر بھیجے گئے؛ ہدایت دینا اللہ کے اختیار میں ہے؛ جو ایمان لائے اور اپنے عمل کی اصلاح کر لے اس کے لیے نہ خوف ہے نہ غم — یعنی ایمان کے ساتھ نیک عمل اور اصلاح نجات کی شرط ہے۔ 2 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے (اے مشرکو!) میں تم سے نہیں کہتا میرے پاس اللہ کے خزانے ہیں اور نہ (یہ کہتا ہوں کہ) میں (از خود) غیب جانتا ہوں اور نہ میں تم سے یہ کہتا ہوں کہ میں کوئی فرشتہ ہوں میں تو اسی چیز کی پیروی کرتا ہوں جو میری طرف وحی فرمائی جاتی ہے آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے کیا اندھا اور دیکھنے والا برابر ہو سکتا ہے؟ تو کیا تم غور نہیں کرتے؟ (ب): جو لوگ اللہ کی آیات کا مذاق اڑائیں یا ان میں فضول بحث کریں ان کی مجلس سے اٹھ جانا چاہیے یہاں تک کہ وہ کسی دوسری بات میں لگ جائیں؛ اگر بھول کر بیٹھ جائیں تو یاد آنے کے بعد ظالم لوگوں کے ساتھ نہیں بیٹھنا چاہیے؛ بری مجلس سے بچنا ضروری ہے۔ 3 (الف): اور جب آپ کے پاس وہ (لوگ) آئیں جو ہماری آیات پر ایمان رکھتے ہیں تو آپ ان سے فرما دیجیے تم پر سلام ہو تمھارے رب نے اپنی ذات (کے ذمہ کرم) پر رحمت لازم فرمائی ہے کہ تم میں سے جو شخص نادانی سے کوئی برائی کر بیٹھے پھر اس کے بعد توبہ کر لے اور (اپنی) اصلاح کر لے تو بے شک

items.a: 1 (الف): اور اسی طرح ہم نے ابراہیم (علیہ السلام) کو دکھائے آسمانوں اور زمینوں کے عجائبات اور اس لیے کہ وہ خوب یقین کرنے والوں میں ہو جائیں۔ (ب): رات کو ستارا دیکھ کر فرمایا (کیا) یہ میرا رب ہے؟ جب وہ غائب ہو گیا تو فرمایا میں غروب ہو جانے والوں کو پسند نہیں کرتا؛ پھر چمکتا چاند دیکھ کر فرمایا (کیا) یہ میرا رب ہے؟ جب وہ بھی غائب ہو گیا تو فرمایا اگر میرا رب مجھے ہدایت نہ فرماتا تو میں بھی گم راہ قوم میں سے ہو جاتا — یوں اپنی قوم پر واضح کیا کہ ڈوبنے والی چیزیں رب نہیں ہو سکتیں۔ 2 (الف): بے شک میں نے اپنا رخ کر لیا سب سے الگ ہو کر اُسی کی طرف جس نے آسمانوں اور زمینوں کو پیدا فرمایا اور میں مشرکوں میں سے نہیں ہوں۔ (ب): اللہ نے ستارے اس لیے بنائے کہ خشکی اور سمندر کے اندھیروں میں ان سے راستے معلوم کیے جائیں۔ 3 (الف): آپ فرما دیجیے کہ وہ کتاب کس نے اتاری تھی جو موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) لے کر آئے تھے جو لوگوں کے لیے نور اور ہدایت تھی جسے تم نے ورق ورق کر رکھا ہے جنھیں تم ظاہر کرتے ہو اور بہت کچھ تم چھپاتے ہو۔ (ب): انسان اللہ کے پاس اکیلا آئے گا جیسے پہلی بار پیدا ہوا تھا؛ دنیا میں دیا ہوا سب مال و اسباب پیچھے چھوڑ آئے گا؛ اس کے سفارشی (جھوٹے معبود) ساتھ نہ ہوں گے؛ آپس کے تمام تعلقات ٹوٹ جائیں گے اور جن پر بھروسہ تھا وہ گم ہو جائیں گے۔

items.a: 1 (الف): یقیناً تمھارے پاس تمھارے رب کی طرف سے (روشن) دلیلیں پہنچ چکی ہیں پس جس نے (حق کو آنکھیں کھول کر) دیکھ لیا تو یہ اس کے (بھلے) کے لیے ہے اور جو (حق سے) اندھا بن گیا تو اس نے اپنا نقصان کیا اور میں تم پر نگہبان نہیں ہوں۔ (ب): جن (جھوٹے معبودوں) کو مشرکین اللہ کے سوا پوجتے ہیں انھیں برا بھلا نہیں کہنا چاہیے، کیونکہ وہ جواب میں جہالت سے زیادتی کرتے ہوئے اللہ کو برا کہیں گے؛ یعنی دعوت میں حکمت اور شائستگی اختیار کرنی چاہیے اور ایسا کام نہیں کرنا چاہیے جو اللہ کی شان میں گستاخی کا سبب بنے۔ 2 (الف): اور تم ظاہری اور باطنی (دونوں قسم کے) گناہوں کو چھوڑ دو بے شک جو لوگ گناہ کرتے ہیں عنقریب انھیں ان کے اعمال کا بدلہ دیا جائے گا۔ (ب): وہ اپنی مرضی سے کچھ مویشیوں اور کھیتی کو ممنوع قرار دیتے کہ انھیں صرف وہی کھائے جسے وہ چاہیں؛ کچھ جانوروں کی پیٹھ پر سواری حرام کرتے؛ اور کچھ جانوروں پر ذبح کے وقت اللہ کا نام نہ لیتے — یہ سب اللہ پر جھوٹ باندھنا تھا۔ 3 (الف): اور اسی طرح ہم بعض ظالموں کو بعض کا دوست بنا دیتے ہیں اس وجہ سے جو وہ اعمال کیا کرتے تھے۔ (ب): وہ لوگ جنھوں نے بے وقوفی اور لاعلمی سے اپنی اولاد کو قتل کیا اور اللہ کے دیے ہوئے رزق کو اللہ پر جھوٹ باندھتے ہوئے حرام کر لیا؛ وہ گم راہ ہو گئے اور ہدایت پانے والے نہ ہوئے۔

items.a: (الف) ترجمہ: اور یتیم کے مال کے قریب نہ جاؤ مگر ایسے طریقے سے جو بہتر ہو یہاں تک کہ وہ اپنی جوانی کو پہنچ جائے، ناپ اور تول انصاف سے پورا کرو، ہم کسی کو اس کی طاقت سے زیادہ تکلیف نہیں دیتے، بات کرو تو انصاف کی کرو چاہے رشتے دار ہی کا معاملہ ہو، اور اللہ کا عہد پورا کرو؛ اللہ تمھیں اس کا حکم دیتا ہے تاکہ تم نصیحت پکڑو۔ (ب) موسیٰ علیہ السلام کو کتاب (تورات) دی گئی جو نیکی کرنے والوں پر نعمت کی تکمیل، ہر چیز کی تفصیل، ہدایت اور رحمت تھی؛ اور یہ (قرآن) برکت والی کتاب ہے جسے ہم نے اتارا، اس کی پیروی کرو اور ڈرو تاکہ تم پر رحم کیا جائے۔

items.a: 1 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے آؤ میں پڑھ کر سناؤں جو کچھ تمھارے رب نے تم پر حرام کیا ہے (یہ) کہ اُس کے ساتھ کسی کو شریک نہ کرو اور والدین کے ساتھ اچھا سلوک کرو اور اپنی اولاد کو تنگ دستی کے ڈر سے قتل نہ کرو ہم تمھیں بھی رزق دیتے ہیں اور انھیں بھی اور بے حیائی کی باتوں کے قریب مت جاؤ جو ان میں سے ظاہر ہیں اور جو پوشیدہ ہیں اور ناحق اُس جان کو قتل نہ کرو جسے (قتل کرنا) اللہ نے حرام ٹھہرایا ہے یہ ہیں (وہ باتیں) جن کی اللہ تمھیں وصیت فرماتا ہے تاکہ تم سمجھ سکو۔ (ب): آٹھ جوڑے: بھیڑ کے دو (نر و مادہ)، بکری کے دو، اونٹ کے دو اور گائے کے دو؛ اللہ نے ان میں سے کسی نر، مادہ یا پیٹ کے بچے کو حرام نہیں کیا، مشرکین کی تحریم بے دلیل اور اللہ پر جھوٹ ہے۔ 2 (الف): اور قریب مت جاؤ یتیم کے مال کے مگر اُس طریقہ سے جو بہت اچھا ہو یہاں تک کہ وہ اپنی جوانی کو پہنچ جائے اور انصاف کے ساتھ ناپ اور تول پورا کرو ہم کسی شخص پر اس کی طاقت سے زیادہ ذمہ داری نہیں ڈالتے اور جب بھی بات کرو تو عدل کرو اگرچہ کوئی رشتہ دار ہی ہو اور اللہ سے کیے ہوئے وعدے کو پورا کرو یہ ہیں (وہ باتیں) جن کی اللہ تمھیں وصیت فرماتا ہے تاکہ تم نصیحت حاصل کرو۔ (ب): موسیٰؑ کو کتاب (تورات) دی گئی تاکہ نیکوکار پر نعمت پوری ہو، اس میں ہر چیز کی تفصیل، ہدایت اور رحمت تھی تاکہ لوگ اپنے رب کی ملاقات پر ایمان لائیں؛ اور قرآن برکت والی کتاب ہے جس کی پیروی اور تقویٰ پر رحمت کا وعدہ ہے۔ 3 (الف): اور بے شک یہ ہے میرا سیدھا راستہ پس اس کی پیروی کرو اور دوسرے راستوں کی پیروی نہ کرو ورنہ وہ تمھیں اس (اللہ) کے راستے سے الگ کر دیں گ

items.a: 1 (الف): بے شک تمھارا رب اللہ ہی ہے جس نے آسمانوں اور زمینوں کو پیدا فرمایا چھ دنوں میں پھر وہ عرش پر (اپنی شان کے لائق) جلوہ فرما ہوا وہی ہر کام کی تدبیر فرماتا ہے اس کی اجازت کے بغیر کوئی سفارش کرنے والا نہیں وہی اللہ تمھارا رب ہے لہٰذا اسی کی عبادت کرو تو کیا تم نصیحت حاصل نہیں کرتے؟ (ب): اس سورت میں سیدنا یونس علیہ السلام اور ان کی قوم کا ذکر ہے، اسی مناسبت سے اس کا نام سورۃ یونس ہے؛ یہ مکی سورت ہے؛ مرکزی مضمون: منکرینِ وحی کے شبہات کا ازالہ اور توحید و رسالت کا اثبات۔ 2 (الف): اور جب انسان کو تکلیف پہنچتی ہے (تو) وہ ہمیں اپنے پہلو پر لیٹے یا بیٹھے یا کھڑے پکارتا ہے پھر جب ہم اس سے اس کی تکلیف دور فرما دیتے ہیں تو ایسے چل دیتا ہے جیسے اس نے تکلیف پہنچنے پر ہمیں پکارا ہی نہ تھا اسی طرح حد سے بڑھنے والوں کے لیے خوش نما بنا دیا گیا جو وہ کام کرتے تھے۔ (ب): وحی اور رسالت کی حقیقت؛ قرآن کا بے مثال معجزہ ہونا؛ توحید کے دلائل اور عجائباتِ قدرت؛ صالحین کا انعام؛ انسان کی تنگ ظرفی؛ حیاتِ دنیوی کا مقصد آزمائش؛ اولیاء اللہ کو کوئی خوف و غم نہ ہونا؛ انبیاء کے واقعات (صفحہ 42 کی فہرست میں سے کوئی سے)۔ 3 (الف): اور وہ اللہ کے سوا ان (چیزوں) کو پوجتے ہیں جو نہ انھیں نقصان پہنچا سکتی ہیں اور نہ انھیں فائدہ دے سکتی ہیں اور وہ کہتے ہیں یہ تو اللہ کے ہاں ہمارے سفارشی ہیں آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے کیا تم اللہ کو ایسی (چیز کی) خبر دیتے ہو جسے وہ نہیں جانتا (نہ) آسمانوں میں اور نہ زمینوں میں؟ وہ پاک ہے اور وہ بہت بلند ہے اس سے جو وہ شرک کرتے ہیں۔ (ب): جنت میں ان کی دعا "سُبْحٰنَكَ

items.a: 1 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے تمھیں آسمان اور زمین سے کون رزق عطا فرماتا ہے؟ یا کون ہے جو کانوں اور آنکھوں کا مالک ہے؟ اور کون زندہ کو مُردہ سے نکالتا ہے اور کون مُردہ کو زندہ سے نکالتا ہے؟ اور کون ہر کام کی تدبیر فرماتا ہے؟ تو وہ ضرور کہیں گے اللہ تو آپ فرما دیجیے تو کیا تم نہیں ڈرتے؟ (ب): ان سے پوچھا گیا کہ کیا تمھارے شریکوں میں کوئی ہے جو مخلوق کو پہلی بار پیدا کرے پھر اسے لوٹائے؟ جواب دیا گیا کہ اللہ ہی مخلوق کو پہلی بار پیدا فرماتا ہے اور وہی اسے لوٹائے گا، پھر تم کہاں بہکے جا رہے ہو؟ 2 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے میں خود اپنے لیے اختیار نہیں رکھتا (نہ) کسی نقصان کا اور نہ ہی کسی نفع کا مگر جو اللہ چاہے ہر اُمت کے لیے ایک وقت مقرر ہے جب ان کا مقرر وقت آ جاتا ہے تو نہ وہ ایک گھڑی پیچھے ہٹ سکتے ہیں اور نہ وہ آگے بڑھ سکتے ہیں۔ (ب): ان سے پوچھا گیا کہ کیا اللہ نے تمھیں (حلال و حرام ٹھہرانے کی) اجازت دی ہے یا تم اللہ پر جھوٹ باندھ رہے ہو؟ یعنی اپنی مرضی سے حلال و حرام ٹھہرانا اللہ پر جھوٹ باندھنا ہے اور قیامت کے دن اس کا انجام برا ہوگا۔ 3 (الف): جو ایمان لائے اور ڈرتے رہے۔ اُن کے لیے خوش خبری ہے دنیا کی زندگی میں (بھی) اور آخرت میں (بھی) اللہ کی باتوں میں کوئی تبدیلی نہیں ہو سکتی یہی بہت بڑی کامیابی ہے۔ (ب): آپ کے رب سے ذرہ برابر چیز بھی چھپی نہیں، نہ زمین میں نہ آسمان میں، نہ اس سے چھوٹی نہ بڑی، سب واضح کتاب (لوحِ محفوظ) میں درج ہے؛ نیز ہم ہر عمل اور تلاوت کے وقت گواہ ہوتے ہیں۔

items.a: 1 (الف): اور آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) انھیں نوح (علیہ السلام) کی خبر پڑھ کر سنائیں جب انھوں نے اپنی قوم سے فرمایا اے میری قوم! اگر تم پر گراں گزرتا ہے تمھارے درمیان میرا رہنا اور اللہ کی آیات کے ساتھ میرا نصیحت کرنا تو میں نے اللہ ہی پر بھروسہ کر لیا ہے پھر تم سب اپنے شرکاء کے ساتھ مل کر اپنی تدبیر کر لو پھر تمھاری تدبیر (کا کوئی پہلو) تم پر پوشیدہ نہ رہے تو جو فیصلہ میرے بارے میں کرنا ہے کر گزرو اور مجھے مہلت نہ دو۔ (ب): (1) نوحؑ نے اپنی قوم کو اللہ کی آیات سے نصیحت کی اور اللہ پر بھروسہ کیا؛ (2) انھوں نے دعوت پر کوئی اجر نہیں مانگا؛ (3) قوم نے انھیں جھٹلایا تو اللہ نے نوحؑ اور کشتی میں سوار مومنوں کو نجات دی اور انھیں زمین میں جانشین بنایا؛ (4) جھٹلانے والوں کو غرق کر دیا گیا — ڈرائے گئے لوگوں کا انجام عبرت ناک ہوا۔ 2 (الف): پھر ہم نے اُن (رسولوں) کے بعد بھیجا موسیٰ (علیہ السلام) اور ہارون (علیہ السلام) کو فرعون اور اُس کے سرداروں کی طرف اپنی نشانیوں کے ساتھ تو ان لوگوں نے تکبر کیا اور وہ مجرم لوگ تھے۔ (ب): (1) اللہ نے بنی اسرائیل کو سمندر پار کرایا اور فرعون اور اس کے لشکر نے ظلم و زیادتی سے ان کا پیچھا کیا؛ (2) ڈوبتے وقت فرعون نے ایمان کا اقرار کیا؛ (3) اس سے کہا گیا اب؟ حالاں کہ تو پہلے نافرمانی کرتا رہا اور فسادی تھا — موت کے وقت کا ایمان قبول نہیں؛ (4) اللہ نے اس کے بدن کو بچا لیا تاکہ بعد والوں کے لیے عبرت کی نشانی ہو۔ 3 (الف): آپ (صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم) فرما دیجیے اے لوگو! یقیناً تمھارے پاس تمھارے رب کی طرف سے حق آ گیا ہے تو جس شخص نے ہدایت قبول کی تو اس نے اپنے

items.a: 1 (الف): اور وہی ہے جس نے زمین کو پھیلایا اور اُس میں پہاڑ اور نہریں بنائیں اور (زمین میں) ہر قسم کے پھل دو دو قسم کے بنائے وہ رات سے دن کو ڈھانپ دیتا ہے یقیناً اس میں ان لوگوں کے لیے نشانیاں ہیں جو غور و فکر کرتے ہیں۔ (ب): اس سورت میں "رعد" کا لفظ آیا ہے جس کا معنی بادل کی گرج ہے جو اللہ کی حمد کے ساتھ تسبیح کرتی ہے، اسی مناسبت سے نام سورۃ الرعد ہے؛ یہ مدنی سورت ہے؛ مرکزی مضمون: عقائدِ ثلاثہ کا اثبات اور ان پر وارد شبہات کا جواب۔ 2 (الف): اللہ جانتا ہے جو ہر مادہ اٹھائے ہوئے ہے اور اس کو بھی جو کچھ رحموں میں کمی اور بیشی ہوتی رہتی ہے اور اس کے ہاں ہر چیز کا اندازہ مقرر ہے۔ (ب): قرآن کی حقانیت؛ توحید، رسالت اور قیامت پر عقلی دلائل؛ اللہ کا کمالِ علم و قدرت؛ نگران فرشتوں کا تقرر؛ قوموں کے عروج و زوال کا قانون؛ گرج اور بجلی سے وحدانیت کا ثبوت؛ اللہ کے ذکر سے سکونِ قلب (صفحہ 64 کی فہرست میں سے کوئی سے)۔ 3 (الف): اس کے پہرے دار (مقرر) ہیں اس (انسان) کے آگے بھی اور پیچھے بھی وہ اللہ کے حکم سے اُس کی حفاظت کرتے ہیں کیوں کہ اللہ کسی قوم سے اپنی نعمت کو نہیں بدلتا جب تک کہ وہ خود اس کی ناشکری نہیں کرتے اور جب اللہ کسی قوم کو تکلیف پہنچانے کا ارادہ کرتا ہے تو پھر اسے کوئی ٹال نہیں سکتا اور نہ ہی اُن کے لیے اللہ کے سوا کوئی مددگار ہوتا ہے۔ (ب): ان کی مثال اس شخص کی سی ہے جو پانی کی طرف ہاتھ پھیلائے کہ پانی خود اس کے منھ تک پہنچ جائے حالاں کہ وہ پہنچنے والا نہیں — یعنی جھوٹے معبود کوئی جواب نہیں دے سکتے اور کافروں کی پکار بے کار ہے۔

items.a: 1 (الف): اور وہ لوگ جو ایمان لائے اور انھوں نے نیک اعمال کیے وہ داخل کیے جائیں گے (ایسی) جنتوں میں جن کے نیچے نہریں بہہ رہی ہوں گی وہ اپنے رب کے حکم سے اُن میں ہمیشہ رہنے والے ہیں وہاں ان کی (ملاقات کی) دعا سلام ہو گی۔ (ب): انھوں نے اللہ کے لیے شریک ٹھہرائے تاکہ لوگوں کو اس کی راہ سے گم راہ کریں؛ تنبیہ یہ کی گئی کہ چند روز فائدہ اٹھا لو، آخرکار تمھارا ٹھکانا آگ ہے۔ 2 (الف): اے میرے رب! مجھے نماز قائم کرنے والا بنا دیجیے اور میری اولاد میں سے بھی اے ہمارے رب! اور میری دعا قبول فرما۔ اے ہمارے رب! مجھے اور میرے والدین کو بخش دیجیے اور سب ایمان والوں کو بھی جس دن حساب قائم ہوگا۔ (ب): اور (یاد کرو) جب ابراہیم (علیہ السلام) نے عرض کیا اے میرے رب! اس شہر کو امن والا بنا دیجیے اور مجھے اور میری اولاد کو دور رکھیے اس (بات) سے کہ ہم بتوں کی پوجا کریں۔ اے میرے رب! بے شک انھوں (یعنی بتوں) نے بہت سے لوگوں کو گم راہ کر دیا ہے لہٰذا جس نے میری پیروی کی تو بے شک وہ مجھ سے ہے اور جس نے میری نافرمانی کی تو بے شک تو بڑا ہی بخشنے والا نہایت رحم فرمانے والا ہے۔ سیدنا ابراہیم علیہ السلام نے مکہ کو امن والا شہر بنانے اور اپنی اولاد کو بت پرستی سے بچانے کی دعا کی۔ اللہ تعالیٰ نے یہ دعا قبول فرمائی: مکہ امن والا شہر بنا، وہاں حرمت والا گھر آباد ہوا اور ان کی نسل سے آخری نبی حضرت محمد صلی اللہ علیہ وآلہ وسلم مبعوث ہوئے جنھوں نے توحید کی دعوت دی؛ اس دعا سے یہ سبق بھی ملتا ہے کہ اپنی اولاد کے ایمان کی فکر اور ان کے لیے دعا کرنی چاہیے۔ 3 (الف): اور یقیناً انھوں نے اپنی چالیں چلی تھیں اور اللہ کے پاس اُن کی

items.a: (الف) ترجمہ: اور ہم نے آپ سے پہلے اگلی قوموں کے گروہوں میں رسول بھیجے؛ اور ان کے پاس کوئی رسول نہیں آتا تھا مگر وہ اس کا مذاق اڑاتے تھے۔ (ب) سورۃ الحجر مکی سورت ہے؛ مرکزی مضمون: قرآن کی حفاظت (اِنَّا نَحْنُ نَزَّلْنَا الذِّکْرَ)، توحید، آدم علیہ السلام اور ابلیس کا واقعہ، ابراہیم اور لوط علیہما السلام کے مہمان اور قومِ لوط، اصحاب الحجر کا انجام اور نبی ﷺ کو صبر کی تلقین۔

items.q: (الف) قَالَ رَبِّ بِمَآ اَغْوَيْتَنِيْ لَاُزَيِّنَنَّ لَهُمْ فِي الْاَرْضِ وَلَاُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ اَجْمَعِيْنَ ۝ اِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِيْنَ آیات کریمہ کا ترجمہ تحریر کریں۔ (ب) اِنَّ عِبَادِيْ لَيْسَ لَكَ عَلَيْهِمْ سُلْطٰنٌ اِلَّا مَنِ اتَّبَعَكَ مِنَ الْغٰوِيْنَ ۝ وَاِنَّ جَهَنَّمَ لَمَوْعِدُهُمْ اَجْمَعِيْنَ آیات کریمہ کے مطابق شیطان کا زور کن لوگوں پر نہیں چلتا اور شیطان کے پیروکاروں کا کیا انجام ہوگا؟
